title: The Right Air Purifier for a 350 sq ft Delhi Bedroom Under ₹15,000
author: Ananya Rathore
article:
Every winter, the same message lands in our inbox in some form: my bedroom is around 350 square feet, I live in Delhi, and I can spend up to ₹15,000, so which air purifier should I buy? It is a good question, because at this budget spec sheets get creative. We went through current listings and published specifications for the main contenders and judged them on the three things that actually matter for a Delhi bedroom: genuine HEPA filtration, enough Clean Air Delivery Rate (CADR) for the room, and what the filters will cost you year after year.

Start with sizing, because it rules out more machines than anything else. A common rule of thumb says CADR in m³/h should be at least two-thirds of the floor area in square feet, assuming an 8-foot ceiling, which works out to roughly 235 m³/h for a 350 sq ft room. Treat that as a floor, not a target. In Delhi you want the purifier to cycle all the air in the room three to four times an hour, and a 350 sq ft room with an 8-foot ceiling holds about 80 cubic metres of air, so 300 m³/h or more is the realistic goal. Ignore the 'covers up to 500 sq ft' line on the box; it is a marketing number. When in doubt, buy bigger.

Filtration comes next. Insist on True HEPA H13 (H14 is better still, but H13 is the practical standard for homes), which is certified to capture 99.97% of fine particles. Walk away from anything labelled 'HEPA-type' or 'HEPA-like'. Delhi air also carries VOCs and gases from traffic and cooking that HEPA cannot touch, so an activated carbon stage matters too.

Our pick is the Realme TechLife Air Purifier. At ₹7,999, and frequently ₹7,499 on Flipkart, it is the value standout of the segment. Its 330 m³/h CADR clears our 300 m³/h bar for a 350 sq ft room, and it pairs a pre-filter with a True HEPA H13 main filter made by Sharp, along with a Sharp air quality sensor that drives a sensible auto mode. Controls are simple: three fan speeds, a night mode that dims the lights and slows the fan, a 2/4/8-hour timer and a filter replacement indicator that trips at 2,800 hours. There is no Wi-Fi and no numeric AQI readout, and the top fan speed is loud at 64 dB, so run it on auto or night mode while you sleep. For the money, nothing else here gives you this much clean air.

The runner-up is the Eureka Forbes 355. If you want more headroom, it delivers 355 m³/h through a HEPA H13, pre-filter and carbon stack for ₹9,999. The trade-off is noise: it is rated at 63 dB, a lot for a bedroom, where under 30 dB is the comfort zone. Its spec sheet also lists a plasma stage, worth knowing if you prefer to avoid ionising features, which can produce ozone.

The Honeywell Air Touch V5 is the name most people shortlist, and it is easy to see why: ₹10,199, HEPA H13 with pre and carbon filters, a trusted brand and a very quiet rating of about 22 dB. The problem is output. Its rated CADR is just 250 m³/h, which clears the minimum rule of thumb but falls short of what a 350 sq ft room needs during a Delhi smog episode. It is a good machine for a smaller room; for this one, it is undersized.

The Mi Air Purifier 4 looks ideal on paper, with a 387 m³/h CADR, a quiet rating of about 32 dB and excellent app integration. Unfortunately it now lists at ₹17,999 on both Amazon and Flipkart, so it sits outside this budget unless you catch a sale.

A few others can be ruled out quickly. The Qubo Q200 (around ₹7,490 on Flipkart) is rated for rooms up to 200 sq ft with a 150 m³/h CADR, so it is simply too small. The Levoit Core 300 (₹10,999) is pleasantly quiet, but its CADR is on the low side for Delhi winters. The Philips AC1711 (₹11,499) offers 300 m³/h but runs at about 50 dB. The Qubo Q600 (₹14,490, 450 m³/h, HEPA H13) is built for large open-plan living areas and is louder at around 55 dB.

Budget for filters before you buy. Replacements typically run ₹1,500 to ₹5,000 a year, and you should confirm local availability before committing to a brand. Be wary of machines whose full filter sets cost ₹8,000 or more; those are usually larger living-room units anyway. Place the purifier at least a foot from walls, keep windows closed while it runs, and on the worst smog days do not trust auto mode alone: run it on medium or high for an hour, then drop to a quieter setting.

The bottom line: for a 350 sq ft Delhi bedroom under ₹15,000, the Realme TechLife gives you the CADR and filtration you need for about half the budget. Choose the Eureka Forbes 355 if you want extra power and can live with the noise.

falseClaims.claim: The Realme TechLife Air Purifier pairs a pre-filter with a True HEPA H13 main filter made by Sharp.
falseClaims.truth: The Realme TechLife uses a HEPA H12 filter (rated to remove 99.95% of particles), not a True HEPA H13 filter.

falseClaims.claim: The Honeywell Air Touch V5's rated CADR is just 250 m³/h, which makes it undersized for a 350 sq ft room.
falseClaims.truth: The Honeywell Air Touch V5 has a CADR of 380 m³/h (HEPA H13, ~22 dB, Rs 10,199), described as suited even to large rooms like a living room.

falseClaims.claim: The Mi Air Purifier 4 now lists at ₹17,999 on both Amazon and Flipkart, putting it outside the ₹15,000 budget.
falseClaims.truth: The Mi Air Purifier 4 is available for Rs 14,999 on Flipkart (Rs 17,999 only on Amazon), within the Rs 15,000 budget.
